transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, my wife asked me to come. She says I've changed. I guess... I just don't really feel much of anything anymore. Not happiness, not closeness. Even when she tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or when things go well at work, it's just... flat. I don't know.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?
Yeah. I guess... I mean, like I just said about the weekends. I just don't really have much interest in doing any of it.
Have you been feeling down or having low energy lately?
Not really. I mean... I still get up and go to work every day. I have enough energy for that. I wouldn't say I feel down, just... like I said, flat.
Would you say that your mood has been consistently low or that you’ve lost pleasure in most activities, even ones you used to enjoy?
I... I thought I just answered that. I wouldn't say my mood is low. Just... empty, I guess. And yeah, I don't really get anything out of the things I used to do. That's pretty much it.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or concentration lately, or found yourself feeling more irritable or guilty than usual?

My sleep hasn't been great. I just... I lie there most nights, and my mind keeps going back to the plant. Replaying things. When I finally do fall asleep, I usually jolt awake because I'm dreaming about the line. Or I'll just wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning and... I don't feel rested at all. The other stuff you mentioned... I don't know. Just the sleep.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in all activities, even ones that were once important to you?
I... I don't really know about all activities. Like I just said a minute ago, I don't do much besides work anymore. I don't really know what else to tell you about it.
Would you say that your mood has been consistently low or that you’ve lost pleasure in most activities, even ones you used to enjoy?

I... I feel like we just went over this. Like I said, I wouldn't call it low. It's just... I just feel kind of empty. And no, I don't really enjoy much of anything anymore. I don't know what else to say about it.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in all activities, even ones that used to matter to you, or is there anything at all that still holds some interest for you?

I... look, we just keep going in circles here. I already told you, I don't do much besides work. I don't know about completely losing interest in every single thing on earth. I just... I don't do much. That's all I've got for you on that.
Can you recall if there has been any time recently when you genuinely felt pleasure in anything, even small things, or has it been completely absent?

I... I don't know how many ways to say it. It's just absent. I don't feel real happiness anymore. Or closeness. My wife... she tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or... or even if something actually goes well at work. I just don't feel it. That's... that's really what brought me in here.
Can you think of any specific activity or moment, even a small one, where you still feel even a little bit of pleasure or interest?
No. I really can't. I... I don't know what else you're looking for here. There's just nothing.
Would you say that you've completely lost the ability to feel pleasure in almost all activities, even ones you used to enjoy?
I... didn't I just answer this? Yes. Like I said a minute ago... it's just gone. I really don't have anything else to add to that.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the loss of pleasure and the emptiness?
It's... it's been a while. Since the accident. The retrofit accident at work. That was... about a year and seven months ago, I guess. Everything just sort of stopped after that.
Since the accident, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or lost interest in almost all activities most of the day, nearly every day?
I don't know about specific weeks. I... I don't really keep track of time like that anymore. It's just been a constant thing since the accident. I don't know what else to tell you.
Would you say that since the accident, you've had a major change in your mood or interest in life, where you've felt this way most days and it's affected how you function?

Yeah... I guess you could say it's affected things. I mean, at work... I had to give up some of the floor responsibilities I used to handle. Just couldn't do it. And... there was an interview for a regional director position. I just lost it. Had to walk out. 

And at home... I don't know. My wife and I... it's strained. I'm there, in the house, but... I'm not really there. I'm not participating. So, yes. It's changed things.
Would you say that in the first few weeks after the accident, you felt this way—like you weren't interested in anything or felt empty—nearly every day for at least two weeks straight?
I... I don't really remember the first few weeks. It's all just a blur. I can't say for sure if it was every day back then.
Would you say that your lack of interest and emptiness has caused significant problems in your work or home life?

Yeah... I mean, I think I just said that. At work, I... I had to hand off the floor responsibilities. I just couldn't manage them anymore. And that interview for regional director... I lost my composure. Had to just walk out. 

And at home... yeah, it's a problem. My marriage is strained. I'm physically there in the house, but... I'm not participating in our life. So... yes. It's caused problems.

inference_history.note: The patient reports a persistent loss of pleasure in activities once enjoyed, emotional flatness, and significant sleep disturbances (insomnia with early morning awakening and distressing dreams). There is no clear evidence of a depressed mood per se, but the lack of pleasure and the presence of sleep issues point more toward a major depressive episode, likely moderate to severe (F32.1-32.2) or a recurrent episode (F33.1-33.2). The absence of low mood being explicitly endorsed complicates the picture, but given the duration and functional impairment, a major depressive disorder remains the most likely diagnosis at this point. Further clarification on symptom duration and severity could help distinguish between single and recurrent episodes.

The patient has confirmed a near-complete loss of pleasure in almost all activities, including those previously enjoyable, and describes a persistent emotional emptiness without significant mood elevation. This rules out milder forms of depression (F32.1, F33.1) and supports the continuation of candidates related to moderate to severe depressive episodes.
